title: Vervain infusion for lactation support
subtitle: A traditional postpartum tea for breastfeeding support
excerpt: A gentle infusion of dried vervain aerial parts, traditionally included in western herbal practice as a galactagogue to support milk supply in the postpartum period. This is a postpartum preparation only, not for use during pregnancy. One cup takes ten minutes. Up to two cups a day while breastfeeding is established.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931) : vervain entry, galactagogue use noted in folk-European practice. British Herbal Pharmacopoeia (1983) : Verbena officinalis, traditional uses including lactation support. King's American Dispensatory (Felter and Lloyd, 1898) : Verbena officinalis, galactagogue action in eclectic herbal practice.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dried vervain keeps 12 months in a tin away from light. Prepare each cup fresh.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb or preparation traditionally used to support or encourage milk production during breastfeeding.
A hot-water preparation of leaves or flowers, steeped covered to retain the volatile oils. The herbal equivalent of making tea.

content.text: Vervain infusion for lactation support is a simple steep of dried vervain aerial parts in hot water, drunk warm in the postpartum weeks when breastfeeding is being established. Vervain has a long record in western herbal practice as a

: a herb traditionally associated with supporting milk supply. One teaspoon of dried aerial parts per cup, steeped covered for ten minutes. The tea is slightly bitter with a faintly grassy flavour. This preparation is for the postpartum period only, once breastfeeding is established. Do not use it in pregnancy.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms. Do not use vervain in pregnancy. Vervain has well-documented traditionally used to ease menstrual cramping activity and is strictly avoided throughout pregnancy. This preparation is for the postpartum period only, once breastfeeding is established. If you have concerns about milk supply, a breastfeeding specialist or lactation consultant is the right first point of contact alongside any herbal support. No significant drug interactions at standard tea dose have been documented for vervain.

content.text: Place the dried vervain in a tea infuser or directly into a warmed teapot.
Strain into a cup and drink warm.

Up to two cups per day, drunk warm. Use for up to four weeks in the early postpartum period, while breastfeeding is being established. If there is no noticeable benefit to milk supply within two weeks, consult a lactation consultant or herbalist for a more tailored approach. Prepare each
Dried vervain keeps 12 months in an airtight tin or jar, away from light, heat, and moisture. Prepare each cup fresh; do not store brewed infusion.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use in pregnancy. Do not use as a substitute for professional lactation support: if feeding is painful, the latch is poor, or supply is a significant concern, a midwife, health visitor, or lactation consultant is the right first call. Herbal support is an adjunct to professional advice, not a replacement. See a doctor if milk supply concerns come with breast pain, redness, or fever, which may indicate mastitis.
